adversarial_requirements: Review 3 recovery pagination: enumerate more than 1,000 unrelated global Checkout sessions and return an exact-reference match on a later page; prove empty/repeated cursors fail closed; rerun open, expired, one-complete, two-complete, completed-plus-drift, provider-retention, and repeated-attempt cases before any attempt advances.

Review 3 subscription-update binding: change customer, workspace, owner, plan, price, current quantity, active status, paid-through, and cancellation state between the service preflight and adapter read; every divergence must produce zero provider mutation. Divergent post-update results must fail before local persistence.

Review 3 provider chronology: inject a provider-created time outside the trusted five-minute tolerance into primary and fallback paths; no signed ready/session binding may be written, same/different keys must not encounter an unreadable record, and bounded later rearm must remain possible.

Review 2 completion recovery: inject first-finalization outage plus expire/completion race and membership drift; same-key retry must bind exactly one completed session, keep every new key blocked pending signed confirmation, and let the notice reconcile current seats.

Review 2 provider-retention recovery: after dual persistence failure and at least 24 hours, discover every exact-reference session before create; expire every open session, reject multiple completions, bind one completion, and advance an authenticated attempt only when all prior attempts are absent or expired. Repeat across more than one failed attempt and tamper attempt/time/reference/provider-created fields.

Review 2 tax ordering: automatic-tax-disabled or otherwise malformed current subscription must produce zero provider mutations; a valid update must explicitly preserve automatic tax and exact price/item/metadata bindings.

Review 2 current-state convergence: first completed-Checkout activation keeps exact historical plan/price, while duplicate/out-of-order notices for the same completed customer/subscription converge status, seats, and supported current plan/price without rewriting activation evidence.
Exact immutable trial: 30 consecutive 24-hour periods, one UID/workspace lifecycle, no retry/sign-in/workspace/email/clock restart, no card, and no automatic charge.

Trusted commerce: only monthly or annual plan keys; exact 200/1200 USD cents per active seat; pending invitations excluded; reject every client price/quantity/customer/subscription/trial/URL/metadata field.

Checkout singularity: concurrent tabs, keys, and different plans cannot open a second session; provider-confirmed expiry, post-provider seat drift, and provider creation plus two persistence failures recover without orphan chargeable sessions or permanent prepared locks.

Subscription singularity: current-provider readback blocks replacement for every recoverable or nonterminal subscription, including unpaid/past_due recovery, and allows replacement only for coherent canceled or incomplete_expired state.

Webhook authority: raw bounded body, real SDK signature/tolerance, current provider retrieval, complete workspace/customer/subscription/price/plan/quantity binding, authenticated deduplication, and duplicate/out-of-order convergence even when provider state changes under the same event ID.

Lifecycle states: only active plus future paid-through grants paid; only active subscriptions receive proration; inactive notices persist directly; validate automatic tax on every provider read/update; test past_due, unpaid, incomplete, incomplete_expired, paused, trialing, cancel-at-period-end, canceled, expired, malformed, unavailable, refund/charge, automatic-tax, and explicit-proration boundaries.

Seat races and idempotency: acceptance/removal reconcile exactly once; provider keys bind workspace, subscription, billing revision, and membership fingerprint; the same retry is stable while recurring membership sets and replacement subscriptions remain distinct; paid writes pause on live/provider mismatch or reconciliation failure.

Free matrix: only a verified active owner user may perform basic interactive writes; members, personal tokens, automation, new seats, foreign assignment, and multi-user writes deny; existing invitation revoke and member removal recover; all stored work remains readable and export-eligible without deletion, while exportAvailable remains false until CT-139.

Member removal: owner only, no self-removal, exact path/body/auth/origin/idempotency validation, transaction-time membership check, HMAC-bound replay, privacy-safe authenticated audit, access termination, authored-data preservation, and paid quantity reduction.

Storage/privacy: direct Firebase clients cannot read/write/list trusted billing collections; raw event IDs, signatures, webhook bodies, raw idempotency keys, customer/payment/card/secret data never enter browser records, events, audits, logs, or errors.

UI/accessibility: exact monthly/annual totals and annual savings, active/pending seats, no-card/no-auto-charge, pre-tax/automatic-tax, trial/free/paid/reconciliation states, keyboard/label/status behavior, confirmed member removal, and narrow-screen layout.

Measurement/scope: CT-133 event contracts remain reconcilable without P-T206/O-201/O-203/live/deployment claims; R-217 operations remain bounded to CT-141; agents, code review, repositories, and PRs are absent.

Manifest: every runtime, test, build, public/UI, Planning, completed-dependency, measurement, config, lockfile, and evidence input that can affect this decision is sealed or defensibly proven outside the hosted graph.
review_questions: Does recovery enumerate the complete time-bounded Stripe Checkout window beyond 1,000 unrelated sessions, reject cursor non-progression, and delay attempt advancement until exact-reference enumeration is complete?

Does every quantity update bind the adapter pre-mutation read to the exact expected subscription/customer/workspace/owner/plan/price/quantity/active/period/cancellation state, make zero mutation on divergence, and reject a divergent result before local persistence?
Do primary and fallback Checkout writes enforce the identical provider-created trusted-time tolerance without signing an unreadable record or permanently locking same/different keys?

Can completion/expiry races, membership drift, repeated persistence outages, provider idempotency pruning, pagination, multiple recovered sessions, or attempt-field tampering create an orphan, a second usable subscription, or a permanent unbound lock?
Does the adapter validate automatic tax and every current subscription binding before any prorated mutation, and does the update itself preserve automatic tax?
Does a duplicate completed-Checkout notice converge the same customer/subscription to current supported plan/price while preserving strict first-activation evidence?
Can any chronology, tampered signed record, replay, partial provider failure, or cross-workspace binding grant or preserve Pro incorrectly, return a provider secret, or mutate protected state?

Do concurrent or boundary-time Checkout attempts create two usable sessions/subscriptions, permit replacement beside a recoverable subscription, or leave a permanent lock after provider creation plus persistence failure, expiry, drift, renewal, or cancellation?
Do duplicate and out-of-order signed notices always converge on freshly retrieved current provider state without trusting event payload order or a raw event identifier?

Do active-seat races and provider failures fail closed, and are provider idempotency references stable for an exact retry but distinct across subscriptions, billing revisions, and recurring membership sets?
Does Free keep all data while enforcing exactly one interactive owner writer and denying every extra-member/token/automation/new-seat path?
Are member removal, exact commercial/automatic-tax copy, export eligibility-versus-availability, state announcements, controls, and responsive behavior safe and accessible?
Are billing authority collections default-deny, all external/payment secrets absent from product evidence, and HTTP errors/order redacted?
Is the 121-file seal complete, including immutable Review 1, Review 2, and Review 3 evidence, are local and hosted authorities/build graphs still separate, and are all prohibited capabilities absent?

findings.evidence: A far-future completed provider session remained readable but prepared and unbound; 25-hour and repeated recovery kept selecting it, no rearm was safe, and the verified signed notice could not reconcile because completed-session lookup required an existing binding.

decision_contract.pass: Every hash and required gate passes, all commercial/access/privacy/manifest questions survive independent adversarial probes, no actionable P0-P3 issue exists, and the reviewer returns explicit PASS with Done eligibility limited to CT-138 implementation output.
decision_contract.fail: Any actionable P0-P3 correctness, billing, security, privacy, accessibility, measurement, build-provenance, manifest-completeness, or scope finding returns explicit FAIL; CT-138 remains In Progress and must be remediated and resealed.

reviewer_instructions: Operate read-only and neutrally. Verify all 121 hashes before and after; independently fresh-read CT-138 revision 10 plus CT-133/135/137 through the project-local API and verify all eight cited semantic/raw backup pairs; rerun every required check; independently reproduce and close all six Review 1, four Review 2, and three Review 3 findings, not only the regression tests; specifically probe record-1001 and cursor-cycle recovery, open/expired/one-complete/two-complete enumeration, exact relative subscription changes before mutation, divergent post-update identity, far-future provider time across primary/fallback and later rearm, plus subscription singularity, lifecycle/Free/HTTP/UI/Firestore/privacy/measurement/hosted graph/dependency/manifest/prohibited scope; do not edit, mutate CT, commit, create provider resources, or change external state; return severity-ranked P0-P3 findings, explicit PASS/FAIL, and bounded Done eligibility only.

review1_findings.required_closure: A recoverable unpaid or past-due subscription blocks replacement, including later provider recovery.
Same-key retry durably binds and seals idempotent open, expired, and completed provider sessions after two persistence failures.
Canceled, unpaid, past-due, paused, incomplete, trialing, and other inactive notices persist current state without proration.
Provider quantity-update references are stable for one retry and distinct across subscription identity, billing revision, and recurring membership sets.
Every current subscription read/update rejects automatic tax disabled, and owner UI copy discloses automatic calculation.
Summary and UI distinguish readable/export-eligible data from exportAvailable=false until CT-139.

review2_findings.required_closure: A completed provider session is durably bound despite membership drift after finalization outage, and its signed notice converges trusted current seats.
Delayed retry discovers and resolves every exact-reference prior session before advancing an authenticated provider attempt; no open orphan or permanent unbound lock remains.
The complete current subscription, especially automatic tax, is validated before any quantity mutation; valid updates explicitly preserve automatic tax.
An already-completed Checkout remains historical activation evidence while the same subscription/customer converges to its current supported plan and price.

review3_findings.required_closure: Enumerate the complete bounded provider window beyond 1,000 unrelated sessions, preserve cursor progress safety, and never advance an attempt before enumeration finishes.

Bind the immediate adapter read and returned update to the exact expected subscription/customer/workspace/owner/plan/price/current quantity/active period state; every between-read change makes zero mutation and no divergent result persists.
Apply the same trusted-now provider-created tolerance before every primary/fallback write; invalid future data creates no unreadable signed record and cannot permanently lock later recovery.
